a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: The query structure matches moclobemide; human single-dose records for moclobemide show rapid oral absorption (Tmax 1.44 h in normal renal function and 1.46 h in renally impaired subjects), consistent with oral absorption.

A structurally similar para-substituted benzamide, sematilide, has absolute oral bioavailability of 47-59% in humans across multiple studies (0.47 ± 0.15, 0.48 ± 0.16, 58-59%, and 47%), directly supporting F >= 20%.
Morpholine-containing reference drugs have measured human F values well above 20%: molsidomine 44-59% and linezolid ~93-100%; bepotastine, a related small molecule, is >70-80%.

L4 fraction-absorbed records for small-molecule analogs show high absorption (levocetirizine ≥85%, NAPA 87-92%, isoniazid 97-99%, bepotastine >85%, rivaroxaban 80-100%), supporting that absorption is not the limiting step.

L5 bidirectional permeability records for morpholine-containing and related analogs show high A-B permeability with efflux ratios near unity or below (SUVN-G3031 0.81, compound 20 0.5, compound 5v 1.0, fexofenadine dispersion 1.10, rivaroxaban weak efflux), indicating gut-wall efflux is unlikely to reduce F below threshold.

The only sub-20% measured F among supplied references is linezolid in mice (18.4%, C35), which is species-specific and contradicted by human linezolid F ~93-100% (C40, C19, C18); it does not provide affirmative low-F evidence for the query.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement for the query molecule itself in the supplied records.
No modified-release formulation-specific bioavailability data for the query or a close analog; modified release may alter absorption kinetics, but no evidence indicates F < 20%.
First-pass/intestinal metabolism of the query is not directly quantified; L5 provides permeability/efflux but no direct gut-wall metabolism measurement.
L5 records are for other molecules; duplicate cards (C65/C70/C73, C66/C68/C69, C67/C72, C71/C76) are counted once and are not independent votes.
Some supporting records are from non-human species (mouse, rat, dog) and are used only as context.
C58 (suppository dissolution) and C63 (hippuric acid rat intestinal absorption) are not directly applicable to oral F.

The only sub-20% value (linezolid in mice, 18.4%) is species-specific and not transferable. Modified-release formulation adds uncertainty but no affirmative low-F evidence.
